speechtext: What about Prince Rupert? Are the establishments there to be abandoned as well?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: We do not own the dock at Prince Rupert. It belongs to the Canadian National Railways.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Does the same policy apply also to the small training establishment at Comox known as Naiden III?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I am advised that that will probably continue to be used as a summer training establishment for Esquimait.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
It has been rather more than that in recent years because it has been

Demobilization-Naval Services
a combined operations training centre. Is combined operations training to be continued there?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: It used to be a rifle range. It is contemplated that it- will continue to be a summer training establishment.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: And for combined operations training?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Is there to be no combined operations training there?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I do not know.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Surely that is one of the great lessons of this war-combined operations. Surely the minister should know whether that is to be carried on.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: There will be combined operations training, of course, but whether at the particular base to which my hon. friend refers I do not know.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I should like to make this general comment regarding military affairs. I think the Department of National Defence would do wisely in making haste very slowly in dismantling our military equipment. I presume they know quite well what to do, but it will not do any harm to have a little support from the house. I do not see evidence of clear sailing for us yet, and it would be well to have our powder prepared and keep it dry.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext: Item agreed to.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Before we proceed to the next item I can now answer the question asked by the leader of the opposition as to authority for the arrangements with respect to rates on the railways. Special rates were established by P.C. 390, of March 12, 1924, passed under the provisions of the Railway Act, section 351.
Personnel suppplies and services, $12,905,279.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Would the minister give'an explanation of this item?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
The estimate is $12,905,279, which represents a decrease from the estimated provision of last year of $14,941,001, and a decrease from the actual expenditure of last year of $4,379,276. The actual amount expended to September 30 last, that is for six months, was $6,416,902, or about forty-nine per cent. The item is made up of clothing, provisions, medical and dental services and so forth. The estimated decrease in the item is accounted for by the fact that, with demobilization proceeding as rapidly as possible, there will be fewer men and women to feed and to clothe, and of course it decreases more 47696-981i
rapidly than pay and allowances, because there are accumulated stocks of clothing and the like.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: May I refer for a moment to the previous item? Did the minister say, order in council 1924?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes, order in council 1924- apparently it has been outstanding for some time-authorizing the arrangement between the defence departments of the government and the railways of special rates for troop travel.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Would the minister table that order in council?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes. It may have already been tabled, but I shall be very glad to do that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I should like to ask the
minister one question on item 5. In the amount under the estimate here there will unquestionably be a considerable amount of personal gear and equipment, boots and clothing, left surplus that has been bought under the various contracts which have been entered into. Will service personnel have any opportunity of purchasing direct from the navy extra boots and household equipment, rather than that stuff being declared surplus to War Assets Corporation?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: No. I am advised that there will be no opportunity for direct purchase from the navy. It was felt that one disposal agency should handle everything.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.
fi. Signal and wireless equipment. $11,402,289.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Does that include any
expenditure for radar stations on shore or on ships in a stationary or semi-stationary position?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I know it does not include the shore establishments, and I do not know that we * have any ships in a stationary position. It includes, of course, items for radar equipment-restricting it to radar equipment-on our ships.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I was referring to a more or less fixed defence such as the strait of San Juan, where we had an international agreement. Has the navy not some responsibilities there?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes, but this item does not include expenditures for that equipment.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
For the radar equipment
there?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I misunderstood my hon.
friend. Not the buildings. It would include any expenditures for the actual equipment
Demobilization-Naval Services

but not for the buildings. My hon. friend is referring to the stations on the east coast and the west coast for directional operations?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: It will include the equipment but not the buildings.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
And the equipment for
locating approaching vessels?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: That is right.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
The reason I am asking
that is that there is grave danger of duplication in this radar service between the army and the navy. While both these departments are under the minister, might I suggest that the matter be looked into fairly carefully?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Yes. * As my hon. friend
knows, that particular equipment, which was extremely secret until the end of the war, was operated in conjunction with the United States navy, and it has continued to be operated by the Canadian navy on that basis. I do not know what the future will be in peace time. It is quite possible that the operation of stations of that kind might ultimately be turned over to another government, if there were a communications department, or perhaps to the Department of Transport. But for the time being these stations on the east and west coasts will continue to be operated by the navy.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I hope the minister is not serious when he suggests that that is to be turned over to the Department of Transport, because it is essentially a defence service for locating approaching vessels. The point I wish to make is, that I hope he will avoid the duplication between radar which is operated by the navy and' radar which is operated by the army in these narrow waters.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I am referring more particularly to the long-range navigation stations. It is a little different from radar. *

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes, but there are a lot of radar stations there which were operated for that purpose. Then may I ask what proportion of the remainder of this money which is to be spent-some eleven million dollars- is to be spent on experimental work. The minister referred in his opening remarks to the fact that there was a research division. I see nowhere in these estimates any indication of money being spent for that research division.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
This item does not include the provision which is made for so-called research and development. I am told that the estimated expenditures under that head are
rMr. Abbott.]
included for the moment under "civil salaries". That is perhaps an explanation I .night have given when we were discussing the increase in the item for civil salaries.
While I am on my feet, I might say that this item includes a very large carryover from the preceding fiscal period, for reasons which I think the committee will understand. A good deal of this radar and wireless and signal equipment is obtained from outside the country, and we had these outstanding commitments. The item shows a decrease of $8,357,045 from the amount provided in the preceding year and a substantial decrease from the amount actually spent. Of the total of about eleven million dollars provided for this year, liabilities of about six million dollars have been carried over from previous years for signal equipment secured but for which settlement was not possible, and, the second head, equipment, which was ordered and delivered for use in the Pacific war. The actual amount spent to September 30 was $1,586,554, or about fourteen per cent.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Do I understand that no money whatever for research work is included in these estimates, and that it is to appear somewhere else?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: No money is included under this item. It is included under item 1, "civil salaries".

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Would it be fair to refer back to that item, then, and ask how much is included under it for research work?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I have not that breakdown here, but I should be very glad to get it and give it to my hon. friend.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I feel that equipment is required in research work, and "civil salaries" seems an extraordinary place under which to put it.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Not for the salaries of research scientists. As I pointed out, the whole question of research between the three services is under the most active consideration. I was at a long meeting this morning at which it was being discussed. It relates not only to naval research. Perhaps the term "research" is a bit unfortunate as far as the navy or any other service is concerned. I would prefer to link the word with development-research and development. As regards pure scientific research, some of it may be done in the services, but I should think a great deal of it would be done under such a group as the natiorfal research council, and in the services it will be both research and development.

Demobilization-Naval Services

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I am still concerned about this, because under item 1 the amount to be spent is only $7 million, which is a very small percentage of the $299 million. Surely, if we are to have a modern navy, we shall spend more money than such a proportion. There must be some mistake there.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I will make inquiries and give my hon. friend any break-down I can as to what amount is included in the estimates for research, but as he knows, it is a fairly elastic item. The cost of research could well come under half a dozen of these different items for the very reason I have mentioned! It is not simply a matter of some scientist sitting down and looking in a test-tube. The work is done in a good many departments of the service, and to allocate a dollar here as being clearly a dollar for research is extremely difficult. The items which one can segregate would be, Jet us say, items such as the salary of an outstanding engineer or of a research man at the head of a research department; but the rest might well be included in the pay and allowances of specialized officers scattered through the service. To suggest that in the navy, for instance, we could have two, three, or four millions allocated for research is not feasible; you have to couple the word with development. It cannot be just research. That is one of those generalizations which can become completely meaningless.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: That is all very well, but there is a lot of experimental equipment; under the head of signals I know of no field where greater opportunities are open under the general term research than in the matter of wireless and signals generally, and I should have thought that item would definitely include some of that experimental equipment.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
To the extent that my hon. friend will include the purchase price of wireless and other signal equipment under the heading of research, I agree with him that it is included here. But I myself would not use the term in reference to an appropriation for research covering the cost of special wireless equipment., even of an experimental nature. I would include it under the general heading of wireless equipment. That illustrates the point I make, that when we talk about research we must understand what we really mean. If my hon. friend means research and development over the whole extent of the service, including wireless equipment., signal equipment and so on, then the expenditure may well be included under several headings as these estimates are made up. This item would certainly include the
istimated cost of experimental equipment. But, as he knows better than I do, a great deal of this type of equipment we must model on the equipment used in the old country and in the United States, and there has been the closest collaboration on the part of the three countries in the development of this; type of equipment. I sincerely hope and! indeed believe that will continue. A good! deal of the cost included in these items is for special types of equipment which we ire obtaining from the United States.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: That is the question I am asking-how much. I realize perfectly well that there are certain forms of equipment which are used generally. They are part of the established equipment. But there is also certain experimental work, and I am referring to experimental equipment which *has not been generally adopted up to date. For instance, take a gun which is being tested out.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I see my hon friend's point, but my answer would be that it is extremely difficult if not impossible to break down the estimates in that way. It is too hard, and cost accounting is difficult enough anyway. I have never felt greatly reassured by people who talk about breaking down costs into water-tight compartments. To break down the cost of experimental equipment in the navy, where the chief of naval staff may have spent some^ time in discussing the matter, where some engineering officers may have been looking into the situation, where the equipment has been made in one of the regular signal departments, to allocate accurately a portion of the cost to research or experiment would be extremely difficult. I suggest that an appropriation should be sufficiently elastic to take care of just that sort of work which my hon. friend quite rightly emphasizes as being so important, but I am afraid I cannot break down the costs and give the details.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: In 1940 the navy department had an equipment division which operated successfully for a period of two years, and it was closed down for some reason, which I have not been able to ascertain. Why was that division closed down?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
It was not closed down:
but was turned over to the Department of Munitions and Supply because that department, as my hon. friend knows was the one which was actively concerned with procurement during the war and was in touch with manufacturers who were making this equipment. The department my hon. friend speaks of was
Demobilization-Naval Services

not discontinued but was turned over to munitions and supply and presumably when munitions and supply's functions are completed it will be turned back if it is still required.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Did not this division
do a tremendous amount of research as well as making equipment for the navy?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I am told that the equipment division was concerned only with asdic n this country.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
The minister in replying to
the hon. member for Nanaimo spoke of the difficulty of breaking down these figures. My experience, in dealing with estimates in a very modest way, has been that the figures have to be broken down before they can be built up. Someone must know how the total was arrived at. You do not simply sit down and fix upon a certain figure and then attempt to break it down; you build up your figures. Could the minister give us a better breakdown on that item?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I can give a break-down,
.but I cannot break it down sufficiently to show in dollars just what was spent on what xny hon. friend described as research. I lhave an elaborate break-down which I shall be glad to give to the committee if it wishes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Let 11s take the question of
research; what is the item there?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
No specific item is set up
for research as such. Included in jivil salaries is provision, I assume, for the salaries of people whose primary responsibility will be scientific research and development, but the other costs are included in the various items: ship costs, ammunition costs, signal costs and so on.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Would there not be an
item for experimental equipment? Perhaps the minister would prefer that name. Surely there must be something like that.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I am told it is not broken down into operating equipment and experimental equipment according to whatever they think might be useful, interesting or appropriate. We have not a break-down of experimental equipment as such, and for the life of me I cannot see why we should have one.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I do not know very much rbout navy estimates, but I had to prepare a good many army estimates in pre-war days and there was a very careful allocation to experimental equipment.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
If we are to attempt to control further expenditures it might be well

worth while for the minister to consider whether in future he should not allocate a certain amount of money under the heading of research or experimental or developmental work, whatever he wants to call it. While I am not trying to minimize the importance of experimental work, may I suggest you cannot go ahead and give carte blanche to everybody to buy, acquire, or trade in any kind of equipment which he finds "useful, interesting or appropriate." In other words, if we are to have control over expenditures I find it extraordinary that that sort of carte blanche should be given to the departments, and that there was not a certain amount of money, say 810 million, or whatever you wish to name, set aside for development and then parcelled out among the various items. Certainly, if that has not been done in the past it should be done in the future. Then we would know how much is being allocated to this important sphere of research, development and experiment.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I quite agree with my hon. friend on this point. Perhaps I should have made this clear. The point which he has made and which the hon. member for Nanaimo has made is particularly applicable, if I may say so, to peace-time estimates. The estimates which we are considering here are in effect war-time estimates. We have huge quantities of equipment acquired during the war; some of it is not yet delivered. We are making no real provision between now and March 31 for purchasing very much more radar or scientific equipment. This is the clean-up period. I think what the hon. member for Kamloops has said is correct in preparing peace-time estimates. There should be a special item put in for developmental expenses; but in war time the item is there; it is included in a mass of others. He used the words "carte blanche". I am afraid that during war it is necessary to give carle blanche or a pretty wide discretion as to the type of equipment and the type of expenditures which they will make' to try to get the best possible weapons, and that certhinly has been done during the war. I quite agree that in peace time there should be a special item, and I think that in peace time members of parliament should see what amount of money the service is asking for under the special head of research and development. I like to include the two together, because then it would include not only the straight scientific end but the work in developing special types of equipment and manufacturing special types of equipment.
I have a little extra detail on this research end which has just been handed to me. In-

Demobilization-Naval Services
eluded in these items, in addition to the strict salaries items under civil salaries, there is a total of $233,355, being what might properly be described as special research and development work, of which amount it is expected that $117,130 would be moneys allocated to the national research council for work which their staff would do.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: It seems such a pitifully small proportion of the total estimates.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I point out to my hon.
friend that this is a clean-up war year. We are spending $298 millions on naval requirements this year. So far as this war is concerned, the weapons are there, crystallized, the best we can get and they are used. Now for next year I do not see that we can give any exact estimate at this time. I am not saying that our people are not giving attention now to research, but these are not next year's estimates that we are considering; they are this year's, and this is primarily a war year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: May I suggest that research work did not stop during the war; it was going on all the time. If this is the cleanup period, surely this is the period when we should be thinking ahead as well and not merely sitting down.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I venture to say that in the amount of money which is included in these estimates we are considering, if you take in the proper allocation of cost of salaries, materials and so on, there will be several million dollars which can, be directly attributed to research and development. I am positive that must be the case.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: That is just the answer I have been trying to get.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
We have slipped, through rather speedily, roughly about $140 millions of estimates. Those of us who are not high-pressured chartered accountants do not have a very clear picture as to how all this money is proposed to be spent. I should like to suggest that we get a little more complete breakdown, item by item, as we go along. We want to cooperate, we do not want to be obstructionists, but we cannot pass intelligently on these items unless we get a little more information.
Speaking to this item specifically, I notice that up to September 28, 'we have spent roughly $1,500,000, and the minister is asking for another $10 million approximately for the remainder of the year. He explained that most of this was for past commitments, which he is cleaning up now.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: All of them.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Would he please break up the $10 million figure if he can to indicate how much is definitely past commitment which we cannot avoid by cancelling contracts, and how much of it is for new equipment that we are still in the process of acquiring. That should be a simple matter.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I can give that, yes. As I mentioned earlier, there is about $6 million worth of equipment on one item, most of it from the United States, of which we must take delivery. If we are to take delivery of it then, of course, a good deal of it will be surplus to any probable requirement in the near future. It was ordered and manufactured on the assumption that we would be operating in the Pacific war and maybe operating in the Atlantic war for a very much longer time than we were. We shall have to take it and pay for it when we receive it, declare a large part of it surplus and dispose of it as best we can. A good deal of it is still very secret equipment, and we shall not be able to put it out into the general commercial channels; we shall have to store it and keep it until such time as perhaps something more modern comes out and it can be revealed.
This item is unfortunately one about which I cannot give as much detail as I should like to give. The majority of the expenditure is for radar and other equipment for far more ships than we shall be operating, and the greater portion of it is from the United States.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Are we not entitled to more information than we have here on the sheet in front of us?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes; I can break that down as between the different types of equipment. For instance, let us take the total of roughly $11,400,000. It is divided into three principal classes: wireless telegraphy equipment, radar equipment and land line communications. The total of the wireless telegraphy equipment is $3,697,239; radar equipment, $8,417,725; land line communications, $284,325. That makes a total of SI2,399,289. We have deducted $1,000,000, estimated as the future year's requirements, which it may be possible to cancel or not have to pay, leaving a balance of $11,399,289. Then I have details as to how this radar, wireless telegraph equipment and the like is allocated as between the different types of ships at sea. I can give that to my hon. friend if he wishes it.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: No; all I want to know now is how much .of this money is to pay for past commitments.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I can answer that question very shortly; all of it.
Demobilization-Naval Services

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
There is nothing at all for
new equipment?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Nothing at all. We are
overcommitted in our requirements for signal equipment. I do not think we can be blamed for that, because the commitments had to be made long in advance and they were made long before the end of the war, but there are no new commitments at all.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I notice in looking at these estimates that $11,000,000 is to be spent by the navy, $13,000,000 by the army and nearly $17,000,000 by the air force, making a total of about $40,000,000 to be spent by the three departments. In view of that situation and in view of what has already been spent in connection with training establishments, would the minister indicate whether he has considered or will consider pooling, as far as possible, the signal resources of the three services, with regard to the signal schools operated for each service? There is a large army signal school at Barriefield, just outside 'Kingston. I dare say the navy and the air force have their own schools, each of which must require the expenditure of a large amount of money to provide equipment to train personnel, particularly with the new developments that have occurred. I am not suggesting that we could have all stages of training for all three services run through the same school, but I suggest that at least the basic training could be done at one point, and I might even suggest that one establishment could have three separate branches. I should like the minister to say whether he will consider this suggestion, with a view to cutting down the very large amount which will have to be spent as long as the three services carry on separately.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I thank my hon. friend for his suggestion, which is excellent. I shall most certainly consider it, because it seems to me this is a case in which there might well be close collaboration among the services. I dare say a good deal of the equipment is not interchangeable; but no doubt, as the hon. member says, much of the training carried on, particularly in the basic stages, could be conducted for all three services, perhaps at one school, leaving the specialized training for other establishments. Certainly I will take the suggestion into consideration.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
What coordination is there
between the three services with respect to this research and development work?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I have already referred to
the matter once or twice. There has always been a subcommittee of the cabinet dealing with research in defence services. At the

moment I forget the personnel, but the Minister of Munitions and Supply is chairman and the committee includes Mr. Harkness of Northern Electric, one or two other outsiders and two or three other ministers. That is at cabinet level. Then the chiefs of staff committee, with the two defence ministers, the deputy ministers and certain technical advisers in the three defence departments have been actively engaged in considering the coordination of research and development in the three services. As I mentioned a moment ago, my colleague the Minister of National Defence for Air and I had a long meeting with defence council this morning at which this subject was under discussion. We believe that within a very short time indeed the three services will be able to make a joint submission to the government as to the way in which research and development activities of the three services should be directed and carried on. I myself believe it is a most important step to take, and I can assure my hon. friend it is being given the closest attention.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
In justice,
fairness and equity I should like to suggest to the Minister of National Defence the advisability of locating this research, scientific and technical establishment to which he has just referred, which I think we all agree is necessary, in the maritime provinces. I want to point out that this government has expended four or five hundred million dollars on technical and research establishments and production of one kind and1 another, of which n6t one dollar was spent in the eastern provinces. Apparently all we are to have down there are dumps and derelicts such as the Cornwallis naval establishment. We have only a memory as regards the naval college, which has been unfairly taken from Nova Seotia and moved to the west coast. In this connection I am going to appeal to the parliamentary assistant for the navy, the hon. member for Halifax, and other members from Nova Scotia to demand that this scientific and research establishment be located in that province. We had no war industries in Nova Scotia until they could not take any more in central Canada. Our workmen were taken away, and now there is not a single war establishment in the maritime provinces with any post-war value. Therefor I make this appeal to the minister, to his associates in the government and to all members of the house to see that this research, scientific and technical undertaking is established in Nova Scotia or in the maritime provinces.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I should like to express sympathy with the hon. member who has just taken his seat. I think the tendency

Demobilization-Naval Services
has been altogether too much to spend money and carry out developments in the central provinces of Canada. We have nothing at all against those provinces, but we must bear in mind that we all pay the money necessary for these establishments and we all have the right to develop.
While I am on my feet I should like to say one more thing-

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I wish to thank the hon. member for Lethbridge for his references to the maritime provinces and to the fairness and equity of having some of these expenditures and enterprises in eastern Canada. If more hon. members would view this matter in that light we might get some measure of justice in Nova Scotia.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: He did not say the money should be spent in Nova Scotia. He said it should be scattered.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I just wish to add that as far as I am concerned we will forgive the Minister of National Defence for any overexpenditure he may make in connection with research and development, but we will not forgive him for any underexpenditure.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.
At six o'clock the committee took recess.
After Recess
The committee resumed at eight o'clock.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: The next item is No. 7, ammunition.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: An hon. member asked the number of officers from the rank of vice admiral down to captain serving or retired since March 1, 1945. In the case of the Royal Canadian Navy, those serving number twenty-six, made up of one vice admiral, two rear admirals, three commodores and twenty captains. Those who have retired since March 1, 1945, total twenty-two, made up of one vice admiral, one rear admiral, one commodore and nineteen captains. Those serving in the R.C.N.R. are two captains, and three captains have retired. In the R.C.N.V.R. there are one commodore and six captains serving, and four captains have retired since March 1, 1945. The grand total is thirty-five serving and twenty-nine retired.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Can the minister give us the percentage of this total of $9,063,563 for ammunition that represents expenditures made already for ammunition. In other words, how much is a carryover and how much represents expenditures for ammunition and bombs of
which we may expect delivery in the future? With respect to the second part of that question, can the minister give us any idea of the amount of equipment of this sort which will be available for training in the future, or what exactly will be done with it? Is it proposed to put it into storage, or will it be dumped into the sea or used for training?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Perhaps I can answer my hon. friend by making a general statement. First, this item of $9,000,000 odd is to clean up liabilities for ammunition procured by the R.C.N. or for ammunition supplied to RjC.N. ships by the admiralty, with a comparatively small amount to replace training ammunition which was destroyed in the explosion at Bedford magazine. In other words, we are ordering practically no ammunition. I may interject to say that we have ample stores of ammunition on hand, in fact substantially more than we can possibly use. This is due to the end of the war.
There is a reduction of approximately $15,000,000 from the estimates of 1944-45, which reflects the fact that procurements had reached a peak in that year. Cancellations have been made progressively, first, after the cessation of hostilities in Europe and, second, after the Japanese surrender. Of the $9,000,000 requested, about $5,000,000 is required to pay for ammunition previously delivered and for which settlement has noi hitherto been possible. Expenditures for the six months which expired on September 30 were $2,299,927, or about twenty-five per cent. I may say that we have cancelled all future ammunition contracts, and the expenditures which are estimated represent no new commitments. It is what we shall require to clean up previously existing commitments.
In answering the second part of my hon. friend's question I may say that we shall have ample supplies of all types of ammunition for which we now have guns for training and target purposes. Following the explosion at Bedford magazine, we have taken the stand that surplus supplies of ammunition, particularly items like depth charges, for which it is believed there can be no reasonable prospective use, should be dumped at sea instead of undertaking expensive magazine installations in order to provide storage for an indefinite period. I can assure the committee that we are retaining ample reserves, not only for any possible future operational requirements but also for training purposes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I just want to be clear on the figures. I understood the minister to say that $5,000,000 of this $9,000,000 is required to pay for ammunition already delivered?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Right.

Demobilization-Naval Services

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: And the $4,000,000 odd is to cover what I would call continuing contracts which it was not possible to cancel?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Right.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
So we may say that we shall have at least $4,000,000 worth of ammunition which has not been expended, but of which delivery will be taken. I am glad to hear the minister say that this will be available for training purposes. In this connection I should like to ask him if he can clear up a matter which has been raised by the people in British Columbia. There is a fine naval ammunition depot just outside my home town, and the citizens have been caused a certain amount of concern following the unfortunate explosion near Halifax. Recently I was assured by the minister that all reasonable precautions have been taken to see that nothing goes wrong at that depot. I thank him for that assurance which I have passed on to those concerned.
According to a news item which appeared in the Vancouver papers, more than half a million dollars is being spent for the extension of the naval magazine at Kamloops. In view of the present cutting down of ammunition requirements; in view of the fact that we are not expecting very much more in the way of ammunition -and bombs, could the minister explain why an enlargement of this magazine is being carried on?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
My hon. friend may recall that when we were discussing item 4, capital expenditures, I stated in answer to a question by the hon. member for St. John-Albert that the estimates included a provision for capital expenditures of some $540,000 at Renous, the eastern magazine, and $644,000 at Kamloops. Following a review of the whole ammunition supply programme made by Rear Admiral Brodeur, who was appointed acting inspector ' general of naval ordnance, we decided a week or so ago that we could cut down our magazine requirements from those which had previously been estimated in order to take care of outstanding commitments, and, broadly speaking, the decision was to expand our requirements at Renous and at Kamloops in approximately the same proportion. We are adding certain magazines at Renous and a similar number at Kamloops, and our storage requirements on the east and west coasts will be approximately on the same basis. The result will be that the estimated expenditures to which I have referred will be about cut in half, and we shall be expanding only about half as much as we had expected at Kamloops, and in the same proportion at Renous. Ammunition, of course, has to be stored under proper conditions. If we have surplus ammuni-
t-ion we are faced with the alternative of either taking it out to sea and drowning it or of storing it in proper magazines. After going over all the circumstances, the decision that has been taken is that by drowning, if I may use that term, what we really believe is surplus ammunition we shall require expansion to only about one-half of what we had previously anticipated at Kamloops and at Renous. The storage at Kamloops and Renous will be expanded to a certain extent to take care of the ammunition that we now have and that will be delivered in the immediate future and for which storage provision must be made.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Before this
item passes I would ask the minister to make inquiry into the possibilities of using the surplus ammunition that he says will probably be dumped at sea for the purpose of opening up drainage ditches in our marsh lands in the maritime provinces. While we in the maritime provinces dislike very much to admit it, we have to accept as it were crumbs from the rich man's table. The western provinces-I and other members voted for it-were granted $20,000,000, or $2,000,000 a year, for prairie farm rehabilitation, and we in the maritime provinces have been asking for some policy that would protect our fertile marsh lands at the head of the bay of Fundy, but no such policy has yet been decided upon. I understand that explosives are used effectively at times under certain conditions in clay soil for opening up drainage ditches, and before this surplus explosive is dumped at sea I would ask. the minister to examine the possibilities of using it as I have indicated.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I shall certainly make inquiries as to whether some of these surplus depth charges can be used in Cumberland county to open up ditches there. I do not know whether they are suitable for the purpose or not.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I would suggest that the depth charges be not dumped too quickly but that they be divided among the various ships in the navy and used as long as they last because they make for very good fishing.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
That is a good point, but
I do want to impress on the committee that surplus high explosives .are not something that you want to leave lying around, stored in the open. If they are really surplus; if there is no reasonable probability of their being used for operations or training in the near future, they just cannot be left lying around. We must either be prepared to incur capital expenditure to provide the necessary magazines to store them or else take steps to dispose of

Demobilization-Naval. Services
them. Naturally I must be guided by the advice of expert ordnance officers in these matters, and the decision has been taken that we should expand our magazine requirements to the extent I have indicated at Kamloops and Renous to store these very dangerous explosives, and that the remainder, which so far as we can see, are not going to be required, should be disposed of.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I was really serious, Mr. Chairman. The personnel of the navy do like their fish occasionally and I know of no better way to get it than by the use of depth charges.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: There is something in that, but I do not believe that that would absorb all the depth charges which we have to dispose of.	.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Our fishermen object to that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Have adequate precautions been taken to obviate such a fright as people got all over this country at the threatened explosive disaster at Halifax recently?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I attempted to answer that as fully as I could last night when I believe my hon. friend was not in his seat at the moment, but he-will see in Hansard the statement that I made. .

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I am not vying with the hon. member for Kamloops for a magazine. I am quite satisfied with having a royal naval college in my riding. But could the minister tell us what is to happen to the joint service magazine at Esquimalt which covers quite a big area and includes several buildings?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I do not know that I can
give a definite answer. I imagine that that magazine will serve a similar function to the one at Halifax, at Bedford, and will be primarily a loading magazine. The main storage magazines will be at Renous on the east coast and at Kamloops on the west. The magazine, at Esquimalt serves the same purpose at Esquimalt as the Bedford magazine serves at Halifax on the east coast. I would hope that the individual storage magazines would be kept at somewhat lower levels than were necessary for operational purposes during the war years.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Does this item include
shells for hunters' guns and that sort of thing?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
No; we do not indulge
in duck-shooting in the navy except by accident.	[DOT]

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.
Armament stores, $24,716,825.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Would the minister
give us a break-down of this 824.000,000?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
This item is to clean up
liabilities for guns, small arms and depth charge projectors, fire control gear and certain modern anti-aircraft weapons ordered for Canadian naval ships designated for the Pacific war. The estimated amount represents a reduction from the estimates of 1944-45 of approximately only SI,700,000, but the actual expenditures for that year were $42,311,787, so that the estimates for this year, as the committee will realize, represent a substantial reduction from the actual expenditures for last year. It is evident, therefore, that the new commitments necessarily incurred this year prior to the cessation of hostilities in Europe, and for the Pacific war, have not been unnecessarily heavy, in these days of rapid development in offensive weapons.
Included in the present estimates is the cost of the provision of certain equipment for the Tribal class of destroyers which are now being built in Canada. I could, if my hon. friend wished, give him some break-down of the item as between the various amounts. It is only by ships and not by classes of particular equipment. Perhaps the statement I have already given will indicate the general trend. It is to clean up. We are ordering no new armaments. Anything that could be cancelled has been cancelled, and in effect the amount which is included here represents a carryover from commitments made during the period prior to the cessation of hostilities. The amount actually expended in the first six months has been $5,604,958, or about twenty-three per cent of the estimated amount.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I understood that
there was some rather expensive electrically controlled fire equipment used on these ships. I wondered if we were completing the equipment with that installation of the vessels which are being maintained, and whether that . cost is included. '

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
That will undoubtedly be
included. The equipment of the carriers, for instance, and the Tribals which are now in course of construction, wmuld be included in the estimates under this head. I have not before me at the moment the break-down of what that particular type of equipment would cost, but if my hon. friend wishes me to get it I think probably such could be obtained.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I should like to get it.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I will see that it is made available. I will get it later if I cannot do so to-night.
Demobilization-Naval Services

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I think the minister has answered in part in his break-down the question I had in mind. I should like to know, however, the amount actually required for, shall I say, current operations. He says that he is paying a lot of this money for previous commitments.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Entirely, I would say. As I have pointed out before, these estimates really reflect plans and comitments w'hich were made while the war was on. From V-E day we started to cut down, but we were then contemplating a Pacific war with a different type of vessel, so that certain new commitments were made for the Pacific fleet between V-E day and V-J day. Since V-J day we have made no new commitments, but we are obliged to liquidate the commitments which had previously been made, and this item in effect represents the fulfilment of those commitments.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: It is difficult to hear back here. This item includes the marine craft; that takes in the R.C.M.P.?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
No. This is armament
stores, item 8.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: And marine craft?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: No; this is just armament stores.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
The item includes rifles,
machine guns, naval guns, et cetera. What percentage of this type of equipment was manufactured in Canada, and is it planned to maintain our manufacturing facilities? I know that certain types of naval guns were produced in Canada. Are we to take any steps to. maintain those factories, to stay in a position where we can manufacture in future our own naval guns?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
My hon. friend has put one of those questions which,, of course, it is difficult to answer. We have a fairly ample stock of the type of weapon which is suited to the craft we now have, but we do not know at the moment whether they are the type of weapon which will_be required in future years. As he knows, probably even better than I do, types have changed rapidly during this war. We have placed contracts for the manufacture of certain types of guns, and by the time we obtained delivery and installed a few of them a later type has come out and we have had to shift over to the newer type. I suppose that is inevitable in the course of any war. The main source of manufacture of those guns has been the industry of Canada; and I hope that in the future there will be a very close liaison,

if I may say so, between the planning departments of the defence services and the general industry, heavy and other, of Canada. It is evident to all of us that in modern war a country depends upon its industrial system, and the manufacture of guns as well as of a number of other types of modem warlike equipment is done by the industry of the country which in peace time is devoted to manufacturing cars and other types of heavy equipment. The plans of the defence departments, as I understand them, are to endeavour to see that the skills which have been built up during the war in Canadian industry for making war equipment will not be lost.
I am sorry that I cannot answer the question in a more definite way. It is not, so far as I know, the intention of the government to maintain special plants to manufacture guns as such. As the hon. member for Vancouver South knows, they have been manufactured by concerns which in peace time make peacetime equipment; and I think that, for any large-scale production in war time, in future wars, if there are any, which I hope there will not be, we shall have to rely on the industry of the country to produce war equipment instead of peace equipment.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Would it not be wise for the government to make some arrangement with the industries of Canada so that those industries are able to keep in touch with improvements made from time to time in different weapons, and so that they will be in a position to manufacture those weapons in the event that this becomes necessary at a later date? It seems a shame for us to let our present industrial efficiency in the manufacture of weapons be lost, and it may be very well be lost unless there is some scheme under which the government and industry will cooperate in the future.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I agree. I was endeavouring to express the same thought, perhaps not as well as my hon. friend did, that there should be a close liaison between the defence departments and the industry which the country would have to rely on in the event of war, to manufacture the instruments of war. I think that, in particular, heavy industry, which is the industry most vital in modern war, should be kept advised of the developments of the newer weapons. I feel sure that no government, whatever that government may be, would neglect taking that elementary precaution. I entirely agree with what my hon. friend has said.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Has any committee been set up or conference arranged with representatives from the defence forces and from industry?

Demobilization-Naval Services

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes. I indicated this afternoon that the so-called defence committee of the cabinet now consists of one or two members of the government, the chiefs of staff, and three or four representatives of Canadian industry. That committee now exists, but as to whether it will be continued in that form or whether some similar committee will be created, I would not want to make a positive statement to-night. I should think, however, that in peace time some liaison should be maintained between either the government at cabinet level or at least between the defence departments and the representatives of industry in the country in order that we may be kept informed of the newer developments in weapons.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Was that merely a war-time committee?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
Speaking from memory,
I believe that committee was set up early in 1940 and it has functioned ever since.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Is there any coordination with Great Britain and the other nations of the commonwealth in this matter of producing arms?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Up to the present time and during the war there has been the closest cooperation and exchange of information not only with Great Britain but with the United States, and again expressing only my own personal views, if I may, I cannot conceive of any war in the foreseeable future in which the United Kingdom, ourselves and the United States would not be fighting on the same side. Therefore it seems to me, and I am sure every member of the committee will agree, that it is of the most vital importance that we should know what the others are doing. We have known during the war, and1 I for one hope that a close liaison will be continued in peace time. It is most desirable that it should, and I am sure every member of the committee would agree with that view.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: We agree.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Returning to the minister's answer to my previous question, I would ask two questions: Is he still accepting deliveries of goods, or still receiving from the contractors goods for the navy for which commitments were made, and has he found it necessary to cancel any contracts or will it be possible to do so?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
The short answer to that is that we have cancelled everything we could, but we have had to take a good deal that was completed. We give notice of cancellation, but it may develop that the article is
completed and as we have to pay for it anyway we might as well take it as pay cancellation charges. We are, however, cancelling everything that we can.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: That is, through munitions and supply?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: You have cancelled all that you can up to the present time, but this sum of money might be subject to some revision and you may be able to make further cancellations or save some money there.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I would hope so. I do not want to speak in the first personal pronoun too much but I have urged, the deputy minister has urged, we have all urged that everything that can be cancelled should be cancelled, because it is only common sense that, the war being over, there is no purpose in going on with the manufacture, but if there should be another war any supplies that we might have would be available. To put it bluntly, we want to get out of that end of it as cheaply as we can. The navy has no incentive to do other than cancel, but if the stuff is completed we might as well take it and see if we can use it rather than just pay cancellation charges and take nothing.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: In the southern part of my constituency there is one of the large producers of small arms. There is a small arms plant at Lakeview, called Long Branch, and it was said at the time the plant was built and put into operation that it might be regarded as the possible Birmingham of Canada for small arms. The plant has now gone down, naturally, because there are fewer requirements such as were needed for war-time purposes. But I would ask the minister, having in mind the importance of production through that plant, whether it will be kept in such shape- that it can be utilized in case armed hostilities break out once more. If that plant is closed entirely it may of course be converted to some other type of production, and all the research, all the equipment and so on which might be needed very quickly at another time would be entirely lost. What is the policy of the government with regard to that plant in the production of small arms such as it formerly turned out?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I would prefer to have my hon: friend direct that question to the Minister of Munitions and Supply when his estimates are up, because, as my hon. friend knows, the primary responsibility for planning and arranging production has been his, and while perhaps I could give a rather general answer to the question I think my hon. friend

Demobilization-Naval Services
would get a complete and much more satisfactory reply from the Minister of Munitions and Supply than from myself.
Mr. GRA\ DON: I shall be glad to accept that suggestion.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: The Minister of Munitions and Supply has estimates in this appropriation, and I suggest that the question of plans for the continuation of specific plants which have been built up under his direction might be directed to him, because he could give a better informed answer than I.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: It is a government plant in any event?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: That is right.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Do I gather from that that the minister anticipates continuing to order through the Department of Munitions and Supply? For instance, I am thinking at the moment of torpedoes. We have ten or twelve destroyers in commission and they will have to be kept supplied with torpedoes.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: For the time being the department of munitions is still the purchasing agent for the government. I understand that the minister proposes to introduce Shortly a measure to combine the departments of supply and reconstruction, and I imagine that in due course the purchase of munitions will revert to the method that was followed before the war.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: To the navy?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
The navy or the defence
departments if the defence departments are combined. But for the time being supply will continue to be the purchasing agent.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I was going to ask a question similar to that put by the hon. member for Yale. I recall, when the change was made in the early stages of the war, I felt that each branch was in a better position to know its requirements and control its purchases than is the case under the system now in vogue. The hon. member for Yale probably had the same idea in mind when he asked his question, ihat the sooner we change back to the old system, giving greater control over purchases :o the department, the better our stocks will be iept and the greater control the navy stores officer will have over his supplies and requirements. There will be a better service to the men. I have in mind a large amount in contracts recently placed in connection wiL. jumpers, jackets, underwear and so on, a list of which I saw about a month ago, certainly since V-J day. If the department of defence, naval services, had complete control, as previously, of purchases the difficulty would be 
overcome to a far greater extent and there would be greater control than at the present time. I suggest to the minister that from a business point of view, he should look into this question and restore at as early a date as possible the old system which I believe operated to good advantage in peace time.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
The views of the senior
hon. member for Halifax in a matter of this kind are extremely valuable, because his extensive business experience enables him to judge how purchases should be made.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
There are two questions I
should like to put to the minister on this item. The first one is a follow-up to the remarks made by the hon. member for Vancouver South. Has any consideration been given to the establishment of arsenals in Canada on the same lines as those in the United States and Great Britain which might combine the manufacture of naval and army guns?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I am not in a position to
go into details in reply to my hon. friend's question. The whole question of arsenals was the subject of a report; and, speaking generally, I believe that a special crown company has been or is being set up to handle the various arsenals, projects which are to be continued for the time being at any rate. But again, this is a matter which has been primarily directed to my colleague, the Minister of Munitions and Supply, and I should appreciate it if my hon. friend would put very much the same questions to him when his estimates come up. I suggest that because I think he would be able to answer it. I know he would be able to give my hon. friend a more informed answer and maybe a more satisfactory answer than I can give.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
I shall be glad to do that.
Could the minister give us information as to who is making the report, and tell us when it will be tabled in the house?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext:
The report was an interdepartmental report; it has been made. The plan which I have indicated as having been adopted or about to be adopted arose out of that report. I do not wish to commit myself to details because I am not informed on them, but if in the course of this discussion my hon. friend would put his question to the Minister of Munitions and Supply I know he would be in a position to give a full explanation of what recommendations have been made, and a full statement as to what steps have been taken or will be taken with regard to the matter.

Demobilization-Naval Services

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Is the minister in a position to give us information as to the name of the crown company which is being set up or which is contemplated?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: No, I am afraid I cannot do that at the moment. Perhaps I can get that. Again I suggest that he put his question to the Minister of Munitions and Supply. Iam assuming that he will be on very shortly in the course of this discussion, and I am sure the minister will be glad to give a full explanation of just what is proposed. I could get it myself and give it in the course of these proceedings. Perhaps I may do so on the army estimates because all three services are interested, but I really think a more lucid and satisfactory explanation will be given by the Minister of Munitions and Supply than by myself, because I would have to brief myself from him and get his views on the matter, and I know he has the thing at his finger-tips. '

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: It might help to get two explanations.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I appreciate the minister's suggestion, and I shall' not pursue the matter any farther here except to say that I wish he would give further consideration to making a statement when the army estimates are up, because I think it should be considered when the defence estimates are under discussion.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I shall be very glad to do that. I will get the necessary information if my hon. friend will let the matter stand until we are dealing with the army estimates. I will consult with my colleague, get the information and give him the statement.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: My other question on this item goes back somewhat to the question of magazines and storage. It has to do with the storage of rifles, machine guns and naval guns. I do not imagine it is the question of the storage of naval guns because they are in a little different class. I shall leave them out for a moment, but on the question of rifles and machine guns, is space being provided in those magazines; they are called magazines? I do not want to deal with them; they might as well serve as weapon stores. Is space being provided in those magazines for the storage of weapons? Further, they are regarded to some extent as stores or reserves of ammunition and weapons over and above the requirements of the immediate permanent forces to be available in the event of our having to call out our armed forces again. Will a reserve be accumulated?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes. The main magazines to which I have referred at Renous and Kamloops are not for the storage of guns or armament as such; they are purely for ammunition. Guns are stored in the dockyards at Halifax and Esquimalt and perhaps elsewhere. There is no danger involved in the storage of guns, whereas ammunition has to be stored-

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: It is purely a storage problem.

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: Yes. I suppose they have to be greased and put in such condition that they will not deteriorate, but there is no danger involved in that. They do not have to be stored in a specially designed type of building to guard against danger to surrounding property. The Renous and Kamloops magazines are for the storage of ammunition, not for guns or weapons.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: I confess this means very little to me in the matter of technical details, but I should like to know from the minister whether this represents our Canadian naval defence and whether in the event of our contributing to a pool for international defence- that is, if under the terms of the San Francisco charter we begin to build collective security do we anticipate diverting part of this, or will it be in addition to this?

speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENCE FOR NAVAL SERVICES
speechtext: We are on the item of armament stores.
